title: HTTP/3 connections do not survive network change, leading to resource loading failures
body: Firefox already moves HTTP/2 connections to the pending list after a network change so subsequent transactions use a new connection, but HTTP/3 connections are not handled the same way in ConnectionEntry::VerifyTraffic. QUIC supports connection migration, and my intent is to handle interface changes gracefully so an HTTP/3 request can complete when a user moves between networks such as Wi-Fi and cellular.

N0.label: N0 HTTP/3 network-change handling gap reported

symptoms_visible: After I load a Cloudflare-hosted site over HTTP/3 and switch networks, pressing “Load New Image” makes the image request fail.
On other Cloudflare sites, links or buttons can silently do nothing after the network change.
I can reproduce this on desktop and Android; sometimes the next request instead falls back to HTTP/2.
N1.label: N1 failure reproduced on Cloudflare HTTP/3

symptoms_visible: After switching between Wi-Fi and cellular, requests continue normally on my Google Cloud HTTP/3 test site but fail on the Cloudflare-hosted copy.
I only see the failure when the network change gives me a different IP address; disabling and re-enabling the same Wi-Fi or returning to the original access point continues to work.
N2.label: N2 server and IP-change boundary established

symptoms_visible: With network.dns.http3_echconfig.enabled set to false, I can still reproduce the failed Cloudflare request after changing networks.
In some runs, the first network change succeeds and the request fails after the second change, when I switch back to the original network.
N3.label: N3 ECH probe collected

symptoms_visible: In the captured run, other-image1.jpg loads successfully after the first network change, but other-image2.jpg fails after the next change.
The first request's HTTP log says it did not find an active connection; the failing request's log says it found an active experienced connection.
N4.label: N4 successful and failing connection-selection logs compared

symptoms_visible: After revisiting the original Fenix scenario, I can switch networks and press “Load New Image”; the new request no longer fails.
N_terminal.label: terminal reporter verified Fenix behavior

question_patterns: Can you provide a distilled Firefox reproduction showing what happens to an HTTP/3 request after changing networks?
What user-visible failure do you see if you load an HTTP/3 site, switch networks, and then make another request?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I load https://<redacted-host>/connection_reuse over HTTP/3, switch to another access point, wait for the change to complete, and press “Load New Image.” The image request fails. On other Cloudflare sites, clicking a link can silently do nothing after the switch. I captured nsHttp logs at https://<redacted-host>/3TSdekj, reproduced it on desktop and Android, and sometimes saw the request fall back to HTTP/2 instead.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The request completes normally after every network change; I cannot reproduce a failure on the test site.
I see the same failed image request on the Cloudflare test site, but only on Android.

edges.comment: Reporter c5-c8 supplied the distilled Cloudflare reproduction, nsHttp profile, desktop/Android scope, HTTP/2 fallback observation, and silent interaction failures. This edge describes only the reporter's systems.

question_patterns: Does the same failure occur with HTTP/3 sites hosted by a different provider?
Can you deploy the same test on another HTTP/3 server and compare the results after changing networks?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I deployed the same simple test to Cloudflare and Google Cloud. Both use HTTP/3. After switching between Wi-Fi and cellular, I can keep making requests to the Google Cloud site, but requests on the Cloudflare-hosted site fail. I reproduced that in Firefox 131 Release on desktop and Android.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The same post-switch request fails on both Cloudflare and Google Cloud.
Cloudflare fails and Google Cloud continues working, but I used a different simple image endpoint for the comparison.

question_patterns: Does the failure require the machine's IP address to change, or does any network-change notification trigger it?
What happens if you disconnect and reconnect to the same network or return to the original access point?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I'm only seeing requests fail after a network change where my IP changes. If I disable and re-enable Wi-Fi, or change access points and then return to the original one, the next HTTP/3 request succeeds.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The request also fails without an IP change and sometimes fails without any network transition at all.
The failure still tracks IP changes, but I reproduced it by moving between two wired interfaces rather than Wi-Fi and cellular.

question_patterns: Do same-network reconnects continue to work?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. Disabling and re-enabling the same Wi-Fi, or returning to the original access point, lets the next request succeed.

edges.comment: Reporter c10 and c14 compared identical test sites on Cloudflare and Google Cloud and narrowed the reporter's failure to transitions that change the client IP.

question_patterns: Does changing the HTTP/3 ECH configuration affect the reproduction?
Can you repeat the network-switch test with network.dns.http3_echconfig.enabled set to false and report only what happens?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: With network.dns.http3_echconfig.enabled set to false, I can still reproduce the failed request. Oddly, in my recent runs it sometimes happens only after the second network change, when I switch back to the original network.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: With ECH disabled, every post-switch request succeeds; turning it back on immediately restores the failure.
The same request fails with ECH disabled, but it happens after the first switch rather than the second.

edges.comment: Reporter c20 performed the configuration-toggle probe and reported that disabling ECH did not change the observable failure. It is modeled as a measurement clarification, not as a solution attempt.

question_patterns: Can you capture nsHttp logs for one successful request and one failed request after the network changes and paste the relevant connection-selection lines?
What does GetH2orH3ActiveConn report for the image that loads versus the image that fails?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: In https://<redacted-host>/3U8H8Ri, other-image1.jpg succeeds and other-image2.jpg fails. For the first load, the log says `GetH2orH3ActiveConn() ... did not find an active connection`. For the second load, it says `GetH2orH3ActiveConn() ... found an active experienced connection ... in native connection entry`.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Both requests create fresh connections according to the log, but the second image still fails.
The same successful-new-connection and failed-active-connection pattern appears, but with different image filenames.

edges.comment: Reporter c21 supplied the profile and pasted the raw nsHttp connection-selection lines. The causal conclusion that stale HTTP/3 reuse is the defect remains engineer-side.

question_patterns: Please retest the original Load New Image scenario in a current Fenix build after changing networks and tell me what you observe.
Can you repeat the original HTTP/3 network-switch reproduction in today's build before we consider this resolved?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I revisited the original scenario in Fenix. After changing networks, the new request from “Load New Image” no longer fails, so this is indeed fixed there.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The new image request still fails in the current Fenix build after I change networks.

solution.intent: On a network change, stop reusing the existing HTTP/3 connection by moving it to the pending list, so a subsequent transaction establishes a new QUIC connection; add regression coverage and verify the original scenario in a build containing the change.
solution.concrete_example: Extend the existing network-change handling in ConnectionEntry::VerifyTraffic to include HTTP/3 connections. Move the old HTTP/3 connection to the pending list so the next request opens a new connection rather than sending on the pre-change path, and cover that behavior with a test.
solution.inference_hint: Engineers combined the reporter's server comparison, IP-change boundary, ECH probe, and nsHttp connection-selection logs with packet-capture observations and Cloudflare's confirmation that it did not support active connection migration. The accepted conclusion is that Firefox reused the pre-change HTTP/3 connection after the client's address changed, while the server stopped returning traffic; moving that connection aside forces a fresh QUIC connection.

edges.comment: Technical resolution from c24 and c26-c35: Cloudflare confirmed that active migration was not supported, and participant2 implemented the original pending-list approach with regression coverage. Reporter c35 later retested the original scenario on the reporter's own Fenix system and confirmed that the new request no longer failed.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted root cause: after an IP-changing network transition, Firefox reused the pre-change HTTP/3 connection even though the Cloudflare path did not support active connection migration, so subsequent packets received no response.

The diagnosis must be grounded in the collected evidence: Cloudflare failed while Google Cloud continued working, failures correlated with an IP change, disabling ECH preserved the failure, and the nsHttp log associated success with no active connection and failure with reuse of an active experienced connection.

The immediate fix must move existing HTTP/3 connections to the pending list on network change so later requests establish a new QUIC connection; it must not claim that the fix implemented QUIC active connection migration.
Must not attribute the issue to ECH or recommend disabling ECH as the fix, because the reporter reproduced the same failure with the ECH configuration disabled.
Must ask the reporter to verify the original network-switch request in a build containing the change and must not declare the issue resolved until that verification succeeds.

persona_hint.experience_level: Highly technical networking and performance engineer who can create hosted HTTP/3 test cases, compare providers and platforms, run Raptor/Browsertime, change networking preferences, inspect DevTools protocols, and interpret nsHttp profiles.
persona_hint.communication_style: Methodical and evidence-driven; provides precise reproduction steps, links profiles and test deployments, corrects terminology when needed, and reports uncertainty or inconsistent reproduction explicitly.
